questions.question: Which method is also known as the ‘Income Disposable Method’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Expenditure Method**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **expenditure method is also known as the income disposal method.**
 
• It's a** method of calculating a country's national income by measuring the final expenditure of all sectors of the economy.** 
 
• The expenditure method includes the following components: Private consumption expenditure, Government consumption expenditure, Gross capital formation, and Net exports. 
 
• **The expenditure method is the most common way to estimate a country's gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• The GDP calculated using this method is nominal GDP, which needs to be adjusted for inflation to get the real GDP. 
 
• To avoid double counting, the expenditure method only considers final expenditure. Intermediate expenditure on goods that are used for further production is excluded

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product method**

 
 
• **Also known as the value added method,** this method calculates national income by adding up the monetary value of all final goods and services produced in an economy.
 
• **It takes into account the value added to a product at each stage of production. **
 
 
 
• **Income method**
 
 
• This **method calculates national income by focusing on the income received from factors of production, such as land and labour. **
 
• **While the statistical data and tools used to measure national income** may differ between these methods, they should all give the same result conceptually.
 
• If the methods do not give the same estimate, it may be due to a lack of relevant statistical data.

questions.question: Which of the following alternatives best describes the term ‘phamsana’ in context to temple architecture?

options.text: A structure of flat round slab at the top of the temple
Temple roofs that are composed of several slabs
The distance between the Garbhagriha and mandapa
The top of the temple where the dhwaja (flag) is situated

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temple roofs that are composed of several slabs**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of **Indian temple architecture**, *phamsana* refers to **temple roofs that are composed of several flat, horizontal slabs**, typically arranged in a stepped or layered manner. 
 
• This style is characteristic of certain regional temples, particularly in northern India.
 
• *Phamsana* is distinct from the curvilinear *Shikhara* style seen in many Nagara-style temples.
 
• The flat, layered nature of *phamsana* roofs provides a different aesthetic and structural design compared to the towering spire-like *Shikhara*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A structure of flat round slab at the top of the temple** – This might refer to the *kalasha* or an architectural finial, but it is not *phamsana*.
 
• **The distance between the Garbhagriha and mandapa** – This refers to the layout or the spatial arrangement, not a roof style.
 
• **The top of the temple where the dhwaja (flag) is situated** – This refers to the *stupa* or *kalasha*, not *phamsana*.

questions.question:
A standing committee is a committee consisting of members of which of the following houses of Parliament?

1.Rajya Sabha

2.Lok Sabha

3.Vidhan Sabha

options.text: Both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Standing Committee** is a permanent committee consisting of members from either or both Houses of Parliament — **Rajya Sabha** and **Lok Sabha**. 
 
• These committees are set up to deal with specific issues or perform detailed scrutiny of government policies, bills, or financial matters.
 
• **Membership**: Members are drawn from both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, depending on the committee's type and function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types**: There are different types of Standing Committees, such as:
 
• **Departmental Standing Committees** (examining ministry-specific policies and bills).
 
• **Financial Committees** (Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, etc.).
 
• **Other Standing Committees** (e.g., Committee on Privileges, Committee on Petitions).
 
• **Permanent in Nature**: Unlike ad hoc committees, these are permanent and reconstituted periodically.
 
• 
 
**Vidhan Sabha**: This is the State Legislative Assembly, not part of the Union Parliament, so its members do not form Standing Committees in the context of Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a primarily Sikh festival?

__
 
• Gyan Panchami is celebrated by **Jains** and not by Sikhs.
 
• It is a **day dedicated to the worship of knowledge and spiritual learning.**
 
• S**ikhs may respect knowledge and education, but this festival is not part of Sikh religious traditions.**
 
• Gyan Panchami is part of the Jain religious calendar and is not focused on Sikh traditions or history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Hola Mohalla**:

 
 
• Hola Mohalla is a **significant Sikh festival, especially in Punjab, and it is celebrated a day after Holi.**
 
• It** was established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji** as a day for Sikhs to showcase their martial arts skills, strength, and valor.
 
• It is **observed with a display of military and cultural processions, prayers, and feasts. This is undoubtedly a Sikh festival.**
 
 
 
• **Baisakhi**:
 
 
• Baisakhi **is one of the most important festivals for Sikhs**.
 
• It **celebrates the formation of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1699** and also marks the beginning of the harvest season in Punjab.
 
• **Sikhs observe this day by gathering at Gurudwaras, participating in processions, and reflecting on the significance of the Khalsa.**
 
 
 
• **Lohri**:
 
 
• Lohri** is a harvest festival celebrated predominantly in Punjab**.
 
• While it is widely celebrated by Sikhs, it is not exclusively a Sikh festival.
 
• It **is also celebrated by Hindus and other communities, marking the end of winter and the beginning of the harvest season. Sikhs,** especially in Punjab, celebrate Lohri with much enthusiasm, but it is not specifically tied to Sikh religious teachings or history.
 
• It is a cultural festival more than a religious one.

questions.question: The proclamation of Constitutional Emergency must be approved by both the houses of parliament within ______________ from the date of its issue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The proclamation of Constitutional Emergency must be approved by both the houses of parliament within **2 months** from the date of its issue.
 
• If the approval is not obtained within this period, the proclamation ceases to operate.
 
• This approval is necessary to ensure that the emergency remains in force and the powers granted under it can continue to be exercised.
 
• The 2-month period gives both houses of Parliament sufficient time to deliberate and decide on the necessity of continuing the emergency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Emergency:**

 
 
• Also known as President's Rule, it is declared under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It occurs when the President is satisfied that the governance in a state cannot be carried out according to the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• During this period, the state's executive authority is exercised by the central government, and the state's legislative assembly may be dissolved or suspended.
 
• This provision is intended to ensure that governance in any state is in accordance with constitutional provisions and maintains the rule of law.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Approval:**
 
 
• Both houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) must approve the proclamation by a simple majority within 2 months of its issuance.
 
• If Lok Sabha is dissolved during this period, the proclamation must be approved by Rajya Sabha within 2 months and by Lok Sabha within 30 days of its reconstitution.
 
• This process ensures democratic oversight and accountability over the use of emergency powers.

questions.question: The Ryotwari (Peasant) System of 1820 was implemented in which of the following regions?

• The **Ryotwari System** was introduced by the British under **Thomas Munro** and **Sir John Malcolm** in the early 19th century (around **1820**) as a way to collect land revenue directly from the peasants (known as "ryots").
 
• **Madras** (now Tamil Nadu) and **Bombay** (now Mumbai, including parts of Gujarat) were the main regions where this system was implemented.
 
• In the Ryotwari system, the government dealt directly with individual farmers, rather than through intermediaries like zamindars (landlords), as was the case in the **Zamindari System**.
 
• Under the Ryotwari system, the peasants were required to pay a fixed land revenue, and the amount was assessed based on the quality of the land.
 
• It was implemented in parts of southern and western India, particularly in **Madras (Tamil Nadu)** and **Bombay (Maharashtra)**.

__
 
• The** biological wealth of the planet is declining rapidly, and human activities are the primary cause. **
 
• **some trends in the decline of biological wealth**: 
 
• The **current rate of species extinction is 100 to 1000 times faster than before humans existed.**
 
• The **IUCN Red List documents the extinction of 784 species **in the last 500 years. 
 
• The **World Wildlife Fund's Living Planet Report 202**2 found that wildlife populations have declined by 69% on average since 1970. 
 
• Human actions have significantly altered **three-quarters of the land-based environment and 66% of the marine environment. **
 
• Two percent of megafauna species have gone extinct over the past 500 years. 
 
• Biodiversity **provides humans with many benefits, including food, water, raw materials, climate regulation, and flood control.**
 
• These benefits are often taken for granted, but when they are degraded, it can lead to unintended consequences. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **In 2010 Wetland (Conservation and Management) Rules were formed for the protection of wetlands in the state.**
 
• A national plan has been set up for the conservation of the aquatic ecosystem. Under this plan, proper assistance will be given to the States for the management of wetlands including Ramsar sites in the country.
 
• **Establishment of Wildlife Crime Control Bureau to control illegal trade in wildlife, including endangered species.**
 
• Different research centres have been set up like **Wildlife Institute of India, Bombay Natural History Society and Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History to do research on how to conserve biodiversity.**
 
• **Banning of the veterinary use of diclofenac drug** by the Indian government as it causes a rapid decline in the number of Gyps vultures.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding fundamental duties?

A. They serve as a warning against anti-national elements and anti-social activities.

B. They serve as a source of inspiration for citizens and foster a sense of discipline and commitment among them.

C. There is no legal sanction against violation of fundamental duties.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B and C**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A:They serve as a warning against anti-national elements and anti-social activities."**
 
• **This statement is Correct**:
 
 
• Fundamental duties **were introduced in the Indian Constitution (Article 51A, through the 42nd Amendment in 1976) **to emphasize the responsibilities of citizens, including fostering unity, protecting sovereignty, and respecting national ideals.
 
• This a**cts as a moral and ethical warning against anti-national and anti-social behavior**.
 
 
 
• **Statement B:"They serve as a source of inspiration for citizens and foster a sense of discipline and commitment among them."**
 
• **This statement is Correct**:
 
 
• Fundamental duties **aim to inspire citizens to perform civic responsibilities, maintain discipline, and strengthen democratic values.**
 
• They are meant to instill patriotism and promote responsible citizenship.
 
 
 
• **Statement C:There is no legal sanction against violation of fundamental duties."**
 
• **This statement is Correct**
 
 
• The** fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning there is no direct legal sanction for their violation.**
 
• However, Parliament has the power to enact laws to enforce specific duties, and certain laws indirectly enforce them (e.g., the Prevention of **Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, penalizing disrespect to the national flag).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duties come under Part IVA and Article 51A.
 
• These duties are statutory and are not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
 
• Fundamental Duties in the Constitution are inspired by USSR.
 
• Japan is the only democratic country, other than India, to have Fundamental duties in its Constitution.
 
• These duties were incorporated through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 in the Constitution on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. 
 
• Only 8 Fundamental duties were based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendation while the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act added 10 Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
 
• Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 was passed that introduced one more fundamental duty in the Constitution. Now there are Eleven Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
 
• Rights and duties are correlative and inseparable

• The **Swadeshi movement was formally proclaimed on August 7, 1905, at the Calcutta Town Hall. **
 
• The movement was a protest against the British decision to partition Bengal, and involved boycotting British products and using Indian-made goods instead. 
 
• On **October 16, 1905, the day the partition came into effect, people in Calcutta called a hartal,** fasted, and paraded the streets singing "Bande Mataram".

• Indian National Congress, initiated the Swadeshi movement in Bengal.
 
• Swadeshi movement was launched as a protest movement which also gave a lead to the Boycott movement in the country.

__
 
• The **slogan of the Swachh Bharat Mission is "Ek Kadam Swachhata Ki Ore",** which translates to "A step towards cleanliness" in English.
 
• This slogan has been used for the past 10 years. 
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Swachh Bharat Mission on October 2, 2014.

• Shri Narendra Modi launched the Swachh Bharat Mission at Rajpath in New Delhi. 
 
• Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) is also known as Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, or Clean India Mission
 
• The campaign aims to achieve the vision of a ‘Clean India’ by 2nd October 2019,i.e. on the 150 birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Under the mission, all villages, Gram Panchayats, Districts, States and Union Territories in India declared themselves “open-defecation free” (ODF) by 2 October 2019, the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• There is the construction of over 100 million toilets in rural India.
 
• The Mission Coordinator for SBM is the Secretary, Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation (MDWS) 
 
• SBM has two Sub-Missions, the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).
 
• Phase 1 of the Swachh Bharat mission lasted till October 2019.
 
• The objectives of the first phase of the mission also included eradication of manual scavenging, generating awareness and bringing about a behavior change regarding sanitation practices, and augmentation of capacity at the local level.
 
• Phase 2 will be implemented between 2020–21 and 2024-25.
 
• The second phase of the mission aims to sustain the open defecation-free status and improve the management of solid and liquid waste.

questions.question: Which river is bounded by Tungabhadra sub-basin of Krishna basin in the northern side and Palar sub-basin in the southern side?

__
 
• The river that is bounded by the Tungabhadra sub-basin of the Krishna basin in the northern side and the Palar sub-basin in the southern side is the **Cauvery Basin**.
 
• **Tungabhadra Sub-basin**: The Tungabhadra River is a major tributary of the Krishna River, flowing primarily through the states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Tungabhadra sub-basin is part of the larger Krishna River Basin, located in the northern region of the Cauvery Basin.
 
• **Palar Sub-basin**: The Palar River is an important river in the southern part of India, flowing through the states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Palar sub-basin is located to the south of the Cauvery Basin.
 
• Now, the **Cauvery Basin** lies in between these two sub-basins:
 
• The **Tungabhadra sub-basin**, which is part of the Krishna Basin, borders the **Cauvery Basin** to the north.
 
• The **Palar sub-basin** borders the **Cauvery Basin** to the south.
 
• Thus, the Cauvery River Basin is geographically bounded by the Tungabhadra sub-basin to the north and the Palar sub-basin to the south.

__
 
• The **concept of the concurrent list in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. **
 
• The** Indian Constitution's Seventh Schedule divides powers between the Union and State governments into three lists:**
 
 
• the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Both the Central and State Governments can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Borrowed from other Countries:

 
• **Australia**: Concurrent List, Federal features, Freedom of trade.
 
• **UK**: Parliamentary system, Rule of law, Common law.
 
• **US**: Fundamental Rights, Judicial review.
 
• **Ireland**: Directive Principles, Nominated members in Rajya Sabha.
 
• **Canada**: Federal structure, Residuary powers.
 
• **Germany**: Emergency provisions.

questions.question: Identify the word that means the minimum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Least distance of distinct vision**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** term for the minimum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain is the least distance of distinct vision.**
 
• It is **also known as the near point of the eye**.
 
• For a young adult with normal vision, **the near point is about 25 cm**. 
 
• **The least distance of distinct vision varies with age**: 
 
 
• **Infants: **The least distance of distinct vision is about 5 to 8 cm.
 
• **Older people:** The least distance of distinct vision increases due to weakened muscles responsible for adjusting the eye lens.
 
• This **defect is called Presbyopia.**
 
• The farthest point up to which the eye can see objects clearly is called the far point of the eye.
 
• F**or a normal eye, the far point is infinity.** 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Presbyopia__

 __
 
• Presbyopia is the gradual loss of your eye's ability to focus on nearby objects.
 
• It is a natural, often annoying part of aging.
 
• Presbyopia usually becomes noticeable in your early to mid-40s and continues to worsen until around age 65.
 
• The ciliary muscles lose their ideal functioning power over time and do not work effectively.
 
• Even the crystalline lens loses its flexibility over time (it starts hardening), thereby affecting its focusing power.
 
• Presbyopia can be treated with the use of simple eyeglasses with convex lenses (positive power).
 
 
 
• ​Near- Sightedness( Myopia)__
 __
 
• It is a common vision condition in which a person can see objects near to him clearly but objects farther away are blurry.
 
• It occurs when the shape of the eye causes light rays to bend( refract) incorrectly, focusing images in the front of the retina instead of on the retina.
 
• Nearsightedness may develop gradually or rapidly often worsening during childhood and adolescence.
 
• Nearsightedness is easily corrected with prescription eyeglasses or contact lenses.
 
• Lenses used to correct nearsightedness are concave in shape. In other words, they are thinner at the center and thicker at the edge.
 
 
 
• Far- Sightedness( Hypermetropia)__
 
 
• It is a common vision condition in which a person can see distant objects clearly, but objects nearby are blurry.
 
• It is the condition of the eyes where the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina.
 
• Here, the light is focussed behind the retina instead of focusing on the retina.
 
• Correction of farsightedness uses a converging lens that compensates for the under convergence by the eye.
 
• The converging lens produces an image farther from the eye than the object so that the farsighted person can see it clearly.

questions.question: A football match cannot be started if either team consists of fewer than ______ players.

• In official competitions, teams are also required to have a specific number of players on the bench as substitutes, typically ranging from 3 to 7 players depending on the competition rules.
 
• The goalkeeper is a crucial position and must be one of the players on the field at all times.
 
• Substitutions can be made during the match to replace tired or injured players, ensuring that a team can maintain at least the minimum number of players required.

questions.question: Article 50 of the Constitution of India mentions about ______.

options.text: promotion of international peace and security
securing the right to adequate means of livelihood
promoting equal justice and providing free legal aid
separation of Judiciary from Executive in public services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Separation of Judiciary from the Executive in public services**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** in the **Constitution of India** 
 
• It directs the state to take steps to **separate the judiciary from the executive** in public services.
 
• The** purpose of this article is to ensure the independence of the judiciary**, which is a fundamental principle for maintaining the rule of law and protecting individual rights.
 
• By separating these functions, the judiciary can act impartially without interference from the executive branch of government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are a set of guidelines in the Indian Constitution that guide the government in making laws and policies.
 
• The DPSPs are found in Articles 36 to 51 of Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) have been amended four times through the following amendments to the Indian Constitution:
 
• 42nd Amendment Act of 1976: Added four new DPSPs, including Articles 39, 39A, 43A, and 48A. These DPSPs include: 
 
 
• Article 39: Securing opportunities for children's healthy development 
 
• Article 39A: Promoting equal justice and providing free legal aid to the poor 
 
• Article 43A: Securing workers' participation in industry management 
 
• Article 48A: Protecting and improving the environment, and safeguarding forests and wildlife 
 
 
 
• 44th Amendment Act of 1978: Added a new DPSP under Article 38, which requires the state to reduce inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities 
 
• 86th Amendment Act of 2002: Changed the subject matter of Article 45 and made basic education a fundamental right under Article 21A 
 
• 97th Amendment Act of 2011: Added a new DPSP for cooperative societies under Article 43B.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only abiotic elements of an ecosystem?

• These include physical and chemical factors such as **soil, minerals**, **water, wind, sunlight, temperature, and rainfall.**

• This option consists entirely of **abiotic components**, which are non-living factors that shape the ecosystem.
 
• A **natural body consisting of minerals, organic matter, air, and water.**
 
• It provides a foundation for plant growth, influences water storage, and regulates nutrient cycling in the ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Minerals**:
 
 
• Inorganic substances** present in soil and rocks, essential for plant nutrition.**
 
• They include elements like calcium, magnesium, potassium, and phosphorus.
 
 
 
• **Wind**:
 
 
• A physical force that affects the dispersal of seeds and pollens.
 
• It also influences temperature, evaporation, and weather patterns.
 
 
 
• **Rainfall**:
 
 
• A critical water source that impacts the availability of water in the ecosystem.
 
• It directly influences plant growth and provides hydration for animals.

questions.question: The climate of India is referred to as:

__
 
• The** climate of India is called a tropical monsoon climate**
 
• **India's climate is tropical because **it's located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
 
• The **monsoon part of the name comes from the two seasonal winds that affect the climate**: the northeast monsoon and the southwest monsoon.
 
• The **southwest monsoon brings most of the country's rainfa**ll, which occurs during the monsoon season of July–September. 
 
• **Other features**
 
 
• India's climate is characterized by wet and dry seasons, but some areas, like the Thar desert and Ladakh, don't have wet seasons.
 
• The **Shivalik Hills region is the wettest part of the country, while the Aravalli Hills is the driest.** 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alpine climate**

 
 
• This **climate has an average temperature below 10°C (50°F) i**n every month of the year.
 
• It's f**ound in high-altitude mountain regions above the treeline.**
 
 
 
• **Arctic climate**
 
 
• This **climate is found near the Earth's poles and has consistently cold temperatures throughout the year.**
 
• Arctic tundra has fewer plant species and more limited wildlife than alpine tundra. 
 
 
 
• **Tundra climate**
 
 
• This **climate has an average temperature of between 0°C and 10°**C for the warmest month.
 
• Tundra climates **can occur at altitude**, which is usually called an alpine climate.
 
• Tundra **climates have some plant life, but the growing season is too short for trees**. Instead, you'll find dwarf shrubs, grasses, and other small plants.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used as a source of energy, when glucose is NOT available in the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fatty acid**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• When glucose is not available in the body, the body can use **fatty acids** and **amino acids** as alternative energy sources
 
• But this question is asked in Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 Official Paper (Held On 03 Dec, 2023 Shift 2) ,
 
 
• so according to this the correct answer is fatty Acid
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• When **glucose is not available in the body, fatty acids, amino acids, and liver glycogen can be used as energy sources**
 
• **Fatty acids**
 
 
• When** blood glucose levels drop**, the body **breaks down fatty acids stored in adipose tissue to produce energy.**
 
• Fatty acids are broken down into acetyl CoA in the liver, which can be oxidized to produce ATP. 
 
 
 
• **Amino acids**
 
 
• When** glycogen and lipid stores are depleted, amino acids become the body's primary energy source.**
 
• Glucogenic amino acids can be converted into glucose through gluconeogenesis. 
 
 
 
• **When blood glucose levels drop, the body breaks down liver glycogen into glucose and releases it into the bloodstream**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactic acid**:

 
 
• Lactic acid is **primarily a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism.**
 
• It can be converted back into glucose via the **Cori cycle** in the liver
 
 
 
• **Carbonic acids**:
 
 
• Carbonic acid is **formed from carbon dioxide and water and plays a role in maintaining pH balance in the body, not in energy metabolism.**
